property_summary: Only the externally-sender address equal to jojoTeam can successfully call newEmergencyOracle (i.e. when invoked from this contract, the call must revert unless c.jojoTeam() == address(this))

newEmergencyOracle(reporter) reverts unless tx.origin equals jojoTeam (i.e., only externally-originating calls from jojoTeam would succeed under the mutant), so for the original contract the call outcome depends on msg.sender being jojoTeam, meaning if the caller (this contract) is not jojoTeam then the call must revert.

When this test contract is not the jojoTeam address, calling newEmergencyOracle must revert (original checks msg.sender), but the mutant (checking tx.origin) can succeed when an external EOAs origin matches jojoTeam — so for all callers where jojoTeam != address(this) the call reverts.
Only the jojoTeam address can successfully call newEmergencyOracle and thus produce a NewEmergencyOracle event with msg.sender equal to jojoTeam.
Only the jojoTeam address can successfully call newEmergencyOracle (calls revert for any other caller).
newEmergencyOracle reverts for callers that are not equal to jojoTeam (i.e., it only succeeds when msg.sender == jojoTeam).
If the caller is jojoTeam then newEmergencyOracle must revert (i.e., only non-jojoTeam callers succeed) — this is violated by the mutant which inverts the check.

For any jojoTeam caller and any description, when newEmergencyOracle is called the created EmergencyOracle.owner() equals the tx.originating jojoTeam caller (the msg.sender passed to constructor) — the mutant that uses address(this) as owner breaks this by setting the oracle's owner to the C contract address for some inputs.

For any jojoTeam caller address and any description string, when jojoTeam calls newEmergencyOracle(description) the created EmergencyOracle.owner() equals the caller address (msg.sender) — the mutant that passes address(this) to the EmergencyOracle constructor breaks this invariant for some inputs because the deployed oracle's owner becomes the C contract instead of the caller.

For any jojoTeam caller address and any description string, when jojoTeam calls newEmergencyOracle(description) the newly deployed EmergencyOracle's owner() equals the caller (msg.sender); the mutant that constructs the oracle with address(this) instead sets the oracle owner to the C contract and thus violates this rule for inputs where jojoTeam is any address (the fuzzer will find one).

For any jojoTeam caller address and any description string, when jojoTeam calls newEmergencyOracle(description) the emitted NewEmergencyOracle's newOracle (a deployed EmergencyOracle) reports its owner() equal to the jojoTeam caller; the mutant that constructs the oracle with address(this) sets the owner to the C contract and thus can make owner() != jojoTeam.

For any jojoTeam caller and any description, when jojoTeam calls newEmergencyOracle(description) the created EmergencyOracle's owner() equals the jojoTeam caller (the msg.sender passed into the EmergencyOracle constructor); the mutant that constructs the oracle with address(this) breaks this by setting the owner to the C contract for some inputs.

When jojoTeam calls newEmergencyOracle, the emitted NewEmergencyOracle event's first argument must equal the caller (msg.sender); the mutant emits jojoTeam instead and so will produce a different owner in the event for some jojoTeam/msg.sender pairs.

For any caller X who is jojoTeam and calls newEmergencyOracle(desc), the emitted NewEmergencyOracle event records the owner equal to the msg.sender (X); the mutant emits jojoTeam instead, so when jojoTeam != msg.sender the mutant can differ — equivalently, after a jojoTeam caller creates an oracle, the NewEmergencyOracle event's first indexed owner equals the caller (msg.sender).

For any caller A that is the jojoTeam, when A calls newEmergencyOracle(...) the emitted NewEmergencyOracle event's first indexed owner equals the tx.sender (the caller); the mutant emits jojoTeam instead and thus can produce a different owner when jojoTeam != tx.sender.

For every caller who is jojoTeam and calls newEmergencyOracle(description), the emitted NewEmergencyOracle event's first argument equals the freshly created EmergencyOracle's owner (owner() getter of the created oracle) — the mutant emits jojoTeam instead, so for cases where msg.sender != jojoTeam the mutant's emitted owner will not match the created oracle's owner.

For any caller A who is jojoTeam and arbitrary description, after calling newEmergencyOracle the emitted event's first argument equals the actual owner stored in the newly created EmergencyOracle (i.e., the oracle.owner() getter equals the event's owner) — the mutant emits jojoTeam instead, breaking this when jojoTeam != msg.sender.

For any caller address set as jojoTeam, when that address calls newEmergencyOracle(description) the contract deploys a non-zero EmergencyOracle and records its address in the emitted/NewEmergencyOracle getter (i.e., the created oracle address returned by the emitted event/getter is non-zero); the mutant returns/address 0 instead, so there exists an input (jojoTeam calling) that makes the mutant violate this by emitting/addressing zero.

For any caller set as jojoTeam and any non-empty description, calling newEmergencyOracle(...) results in NewEmergencyOracle emitting a non-zero oracle address in the correct (reference) contract; the mutant emits/address 0 instead for some inputs (when creation is simulated to fail).

For any jojoTeam address calling newEmergencyOracle with any description, the reference contract emits a NewEmergencyOracle event whose newOracle argument is non-zero (a freshly deployed EmergencyOracle); the mutant can emit zero instead, so there exists inputs (jojoTeam caller) where mutant produces newOracle == address(0) violating this rule.

For any jojoTeam address that calls newEmergencyOracle with any description, the reference contract emits a non-zero newOracle address (a freshly deployed EmergencyOracle) and thus the emitted/new oracle address observed via a post-call getter/event behavior is non-zero; the mutant sometimes emits/address 0, violating this rule.

For any jojoTeam address that calls newEmergencyOracle(description), the reference contract always emits/produces a non-zero newOracle address (a freshly deployed EmergencyOracle) — the mutant can produce/address zero, violating this.
